title: Before You Buy Off-Plan, Ask: Who Will Buy This Unit From Me?

keywords: how to pick a presale unit
body:
Most investors walk into an off-plan deal with one question in mind: how much does it cost? It is a fair question, but it is the wrong place to start. The question that decides whether you make money is a different one: who will buy this from me?

## Why the price is not the whole story

When you buy a unit before it is built and plan to sell before completion, you are not the end user. You are a middle step. At some point you will assign your contract to someone else, and that person has to want the unit enough to pay you more than you paid.

So the price you pay today only tells you half of the deal. The other half is the buyer who comes after you. If that buyer does not show up, a cheap entry price does not help you at all.

## When you assign, you need the next buyer

An assignment is a sale. Like any sale, it needs demand. Before you sign, try to picture the person who will take the contract off your hands:

- Would they live in it, or rent it out?
- What would make them choose your unit over the others still available in the same building?
- Would they pay a premium for it, or would they wait for a discount?

If you cannot picture that buyer clearly, that is a warning sign.

## The units everybody wants sell fast

In my experience, the units that resell quickly are the ones most people would pick anyway. A good layout. A good view. A size that fits what most buyers in that market are looking for.

The units that wait are the unusual ones. A strange layout that is hard to furnish. A bad view onto a wall or a parking area. A floor plan that only works for a very specific kind of buyer. These units can look like a bargain on the price list, but they are often cheaper for a reason, and the next buyer will notice the same thing you did.

## A simple check before you sign

Before you commit to an off-plan unit, run through these steps:

1. **Ask who the next buyer is.** Describe that person in one sentence.
2. **Compare the unit to the rest of the building.** Is it one of the units most people would want, or one they would skip?
3. **Look at the layout and the view honestly.** If either one would make you hesitate as an end user, it will make the next buyer hesitate too.
4. **Think about the wait.** If the unit takes longer to sell, can you hold it until the right buyer appears?

## Where the profit really comes from

You do not make money on the day you buy. You make money on the day someone else wants the unit more than you did. Choose the unit with that person in mind, and the price question becomes much easier to answer. This is my opinion based on how I see these deals work, not financial advice, so always check the assignment rules in your own contract and market.

faq: What does it mean to assign an off-plan contract?
It means you transfer your purchase contract to a new buyer before the building is finished, usually for more than you paid. The rules and fees depend on your contract and your market.
Which presale units are easiest to resell?
The units most buyers would choose anyway, with a practical layout and a good view, tend to resell fastest. Unusual layouts and poor views usually take longer to find a buyer.
Is the cheapest off-plan unit the best investment?
Not always. A low price can reflect a weak layout or a bad view, and the next buyer will see the same weakness. Think about who will buy it from you before you focus on price.
